'''Cev Rees''' was a child who once accompanied the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Thannik]], his [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[GT-9R]], the outlaw [[Dirk Harkness]], and a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] named [[Rhen]] to the [[Dancing Dewback]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]]. Rees was with the same group during an attempt to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] several crates of [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].

==Biography==
Cev Rees once accompanied the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Thannik]] on a visit to the [[Dancing Dewback]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]], where Thannik intended to meet with a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] contact. Also present in Thannik's party were his [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[GT-9R]], the outlaw [[Dirk Harkness]], and a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] named [[Rhen]]. While Thannik and GT-9R hung back to assess the crowd for possible trouble, Rees accompanied Rhen and Harkness on their way to the bar.<ref name="Revised" />

Rees caused Rhen some trouble when he picked the pocket of [[Fenn (spacer)|Fenn]], one of the [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] at the bar. When Fenn noticed his wallet was missing, he found Rhen holding it as Rees melted into the crowd. Rhen claimed he had dropped it, and offered the burly spacer a drink in order to avoid any possible confrontation.<ref name="Revised" />

Rees was also with the same group (minus Harkness) when they attempted to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] several crates of [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], only to be accosted by a group who claimed Thannik and his associates owed them money. These pursuers caught up with Thannik and his companions in an open-air market on a [[Planet/Legends|world]] with a bright blue [[Star/Legends|sun]]. Three of them, led by a tall, cloaked Human, pulled their blasters on the group and demanded their money. Thannik opened fire, wounding the leader, and avoided the return fire. In the meantime, his companions fled to a nearby cantina, where they found themselves surrounded by more armed individuals.<ref name="Revised" />

==Behind the scenes==
Both of Rees' appearances are game play examples in [[Bill Smith]]'s [[1996]] roleplaying game book ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]'', published by [[West End Games]]. These rulebook examples are rewritten versions of examples previously included in Smith's [[1992]] game book ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition]]''. The original second edition examples do not feature Rees. Instead, the visit to the Dancing Dewback features only GT-9R and a different bounty hunter named [[Tirog]], while the marketplace encounter features GT-9R, Tirog, a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] named [[Drebble]], and a child known only as [[Ace (kid)|Ace]].

If the statistics for the "Kid" template in the revised edition rulebook apply to Rees, he is a twelve-[[Standard year/Legends|year]]-old [[Human/Legends|Human]], whose meager possessions include two bottles of [[fizzyglug]], a bag of candy, a small stone, some string, 25 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], and a small pet which may or may not be dead.
